findings.claim: A KnowDesign packaged launch without OD_BUILD_PROFILE still resolves to the Open Design brand, so the required baked KnowDesign identity is not satisfied.
findings.evidence: Acceptance criteria D-020 require the profile to be baked so "a launch with no environment variable is knowdesign", but `resolveBrand(env = process.env)` returns `KNOWDESIGN_BRAND` only when `OD_BUILD_PROFILE` is exactly `knowdesign`, otherwise `OPEN_DESIGN_BRAND`.
findings.suggested_fix: Thread the baked packaged brand/config into brand resolution for packaged runtime paths, or generate/package a brand config that makes KnowDesign the default without relying on OD_BUILD_PROFILE.

findings.claim: The web brand runtime is not driven from the mandated single brand descriptor in packages/release/src/brand.ts.
findings.evidence: Acceptance criteria require observable identity to be driven from ONE brand descriptor in `packages/release/src/brand.ts`, but this file imports `KNOWDESIGN_BRAND`, `OPEN_DESIGN_BRAND`, `BrandDescriptor`, and `BuildProfile` from `@open-design/contracts` instead of the new release descriptor.
findings.suggested_fix: Expose/reuse the `packages/release/src/brand.ts` descriptor for web code or generate the web-facing descriptor from that single source of truth.

findings.claim: A request with an already-exited peer still opens a socket before rejecting, so it can touch a stale or wrong IPC endpoint despite the peer having already failed.
findings.evidence: `requestJsonIpc` calls `const socket = createConnection(socketPath)` before checking `if (peer.exitCode != null || peer.signalCode != null)` later in the same function; D-021 requires IPC requests to end on observed peer exit.
findings.suggested_fix: Check `peer.exitCode`/`peer.signalCode` before creating the connection and reject immediately when the peer has already exited.

findings.claim: Startup events are globally sorted by per-process sequence number, which can misorder a JSONL log containing events from multiple writer processes.
findings.evidence: `StartupEvent.seq` is documented as "1-based order in which the writing process passed its phases", but `parseStartupEvents` returns `events.sort((a, b) => a.seq - b.seq)` and `lastStartupEvent` then treats the sorted array's last element as latest.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve file order for cross-process JSONL ordering, or sort by a globally monotonic field; if `seq` is only per-pid, do not use it to determine the latest event across pids.
